'''William James Macdonald [[Fellowship of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]]''' was born on 14 December 1851 in [[Scotland]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=William James Macdonald - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Macdonald_William/ |access-date=2022-06-23 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref> He is known for being a pioneer of the introduction of modern [[geometry]] to the mathematical curriculum in schools and for being one of the founding members of the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Macdonald |first=W. J. |date=1888 |title=Office-Bearers |journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=7 |pages=1 |doi=10.1017/S0013091500030200 |s2cid=251062914 |issn=0013-0915|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=EMS Founder Members |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/EMS/EMSFounder/ |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Macdonald was born in [[Huntly]], [[Aberdeenshire]], but moved to the coastal town of [[St Andrews]] when he was young.<ref name=":0" /> There he got an education in [[Madras College]],<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Biographies |url=http://www.madrascollegearchive.org.uk/Pupils/biographies/former/fps/williamjamesmacdonald.htm |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=www.madrascollegearchive.org.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=MCM Christmas 1912 |url=http://www.madrascollegearchive.org.uk/journals/mcm/mcm%20621/mcm%20621.htm |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=www.madrascollegearchive.org.uk}}</ref> and became dux of the college in 1868.<ref name=":0" />

After completing his school education, he entered the [[University of St Andrews]], where he studied a variety of subjects including [[mathematics]], [[English literature]], [[Latin]], [[Greek language|Greek]], [[chemistry]], and [[philosophy]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Biographical Register 1747-1897 |url=https://arts.st-andrews.ac.uk/biographical-register/data/documents/1393890924 |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=arts.st-andrews.ac.uk}}</ref> While there Macdonald won many prizes, including the Miller prize given to the student who did the best work in 1870, 1871, and 1872, the Gray prize in 1872 for an essay on spectrum analysis, and the Arnott prize, also in 1872.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

After graduating, Macdonald was appointed assistant to the Mathematics Department in Madras College, but only taught there for a short time before accepting a role as Mathematics Master at [[Merchiston Castle School|Merchiston Castle school]] in [[Edinburgh]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> He soon after accepted a role at [[Daniel Stewart’s College]] where he spent the rest of his career.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> 

Between 1898 and 1899, he was the president of the [[Scottish Secondary Teachers' Association]].<ref name=":0" />

He died in Edinburgh on 29 December 1941.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

== Accomplishments ==
Macdonald was a pioneer in the ''introduction of modern geometry'' to the mathematical [[curriculum]]. He wrote ''Higher Geometry: Containing an Introduction to Modern Geometry and Elementary Geometrical Conics,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Macdonald |first=William James |title=Higher Geometry: Containing an Introduction to Modern Geometry and Elementary Geometrical Conics |publisher=James Thin |year=1897 |edition=2nd |location=Edinburgh}}</ref>'' a text which was widely used in schools and colleges to teach geometry.<ref name=":0" />

He was a founding member of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> and was honoured by the society when he was elected as president for 1887-88 session.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rankin |first=R. A. |title=The first hundred years (1883–1983) |journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society |year=1983 |language=en |volume=26 |issue=2 |pages=147 |doi=10.1017/S0013091500016849 |s2cid=178104090 |issn=0013-0915|doi-access=free }}</ref>

On the 1st of February 1886, he accepted a fellowship to the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]<ref>{{Cite book |last=Royal Society of Edinburgh |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C7k9AQAAMAAJ&q=macdonald |title=Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh |year=1886 |edition=Volume 13 |location=Edinburgh |pages=596}}</ref> after being proposed by William Swan, John Sturgeon Mackay, George Chrystal, and Sir Thomas Muir.<ref name=":0" />

In June 1914, he was offered the degree of LL.D by the Senatus Academicus of the University of St Andrews, but he respectfully declined the honour.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
